
=================================================================
#39 Jolbon  (-37)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: Part II — The Dawn of War / The Seventh Invasion · place: jolbon · tone: founder fairy tale
Logline: He’s still wet from the river when the spears find him. The chieftain’s daughter is sharper than the spears.
=================================================================
[0] ── SCENE: The Scouts ──
[1] ¶ He is still wet from the river when the pines stop being empty. Two men in Yeon leather, spears too casual to be hunting, too careful to be lost. Jolbon scouts find him first. The bow is already in the pine needles. His hands are empty and shaking anyway.
[2] [PLACE jolbon: Pine valleys, crow clans, and nobody waiting for a king.]
[3] [MAP -37: From a borrowed stable to a valley of five roofs. The turtles handled the middle part.]
[4] Scout: Stop— stop stop— / Bow—
[5] Second scout: I got him I got— / Red. That’s not ours.
[6] Jumong: Down. It’s down. / Don’t— spear. Please. / Water—
[7] Scout: Hands. Hands where I can see. / You deaf?
[8] Jumong: Yeah. Yeah look. / Just— I ran. River. That’s it.
[9] Second scout: Name. Fast. / If Tabal has to come out here I’m blaming you.
[10] Jumong: Jumong. / Jumong. That’s— that’s the name.
[11] ¶ They bring him in at dusk, not as a guest. One scout keeps looking back like the pines might grow more men. The valley opens under grey giwa. On the porch **Yeon Tabal**, chieftain of Jolbon, holds a cup he is not drinking.
[12] ── SCENE: Tabal’s Hall ──
[13] ¶ Tabal walks him across the packed earth like a man showing a storeroom to a thief: grain porch, well, pine, five roofs that will not share a yard.
[14] [CARD Yeon Tabal: The chief of Jolbon. He shows thieves his storeroom on purpose.]
[15] ¶ Inside, the hall is torches and a man who has not offered a mat. They put Jumong on his knees, packed earth in the weave of his red silk. He tries a grin. It does not survive the torches.
[16] Yeon Tabal: So who sent you.
[17] Jumong: Nobody sent me. / Your men grabbed me. I was just— here.
[18] Yeon Tabal: I asked for a name.
[19] Jumong: Jumong. / That’s the name.
[20] Yeon Tabal: Your clothes don’t look like anything nearby. / Mohe? Khitan? Or the commandery?
[21] ¶ At Tabal’s shoulder stands a woman in dusty-rose silk with a tally-stick in her hand. She has not looked at him once.
[22] Jumong: Pretty. Just—
[23] Yeon Tabal: Eyes. Front.
[24] Sosuno: Count the dirt. / Not him.
[25] Jumong: Ow— I said it.
[26] ¶ Tabal notices the bow. The wood is wrong for every hand in the room except one.
[27] ¶ They put Jumong’s bow in Tabal’s hands. He cannot pull the string, and the limb does not do him the courtesy of bending.
[28] Yeon Tabal: Stop! / Hands off him. / …Whose son are you.
[29] Jumong: Son of Haemosu. / The bow knows. I didn’t ask it to.
[30] ¶ He gives it back, and the wood stays as it was, which is worse than if it had snapped.
[31] Yeon Tabal: Wife?
[32] Jumong: …One. In Buyeo. She told me to run. / So I ran.
[33] ¶ At her father’s shoulder, the woman with the tally-stick makes a small mark she did not need to make.
[34] Yeon Tabal: You're a slave. My daughter's. / Shed. You hunt, you eat. / I do not want ash tracked into my hall.
[35] ¶ For a week Tabal uses him like a tool he has not paid for. West millet has a boar. Two cousins have a ditch and a knife each. Jumong hits both problems and sits in the dirt until someone tells him to stand. Tabal does not thank him. He just stops inventing work.
[36] Yeon Tabal: The millet likes you. I don’t. / Stay anyway. / Shed stays the shed.
[37] Jumong: Yes sir. / …The well’s nicer though.
[38] Yeon Tabal: Then go fetch. Out.
[39] ── SCENE: The Hunt Muster ──
[40] ¶ Tabal’s daughter **Sosuno**, a widow, is already on the grain porch, running Jolbon before she has priced the exile: spear-count, west line, who eats, who rides. The yard answers her first and her father second.
[41] [CARD Sosuno: Tabal’s daughter. She has priced every man in the yard, and she has not finished with this one.]
[42] Sosuno: West line. Two short. / You. Spear. Not that one, the one that isn’t bent. / We leave at first light. If you’re late I leave you.
[43] A hunter: Yes—
[44] Sosuno: Not yes. The count. / East, you’re overlapping. Split. / If I have to say it twice you sit the hunt out.
[45] A hunter: —Split. Sorry.
[46] ¶ Then the wet man is in the yard. Red silk. A back she has not counted. The yard goes quiet. Nobody dropped a spear. They just stopped being loud, because she did.
[47] ¶ Something in her goes stupid while the chin stays up. His father’s name she heard in the hall and filed under nonsense. The line of a shoulder she cannot file anywhere. She will deny all of this to the millet.
[48] Sosuno: …Next. / I said next. / Don’t look at me. Look at the line.
[49] Yeon Tabal: Sosuno. / The line.
[50] Sosuno: I have the line. / West is short two. I said that. / Sun’s in my eyes.
[51] ¶ She starts calling him names because looking is worse. **Big idiot** is the one that sticks. He answers to it on the third day, cheerful, which makes it worse.
[52] ¶ Soon the porch has a name for him too: Sosuno’s worker. She hates how easily it fits.
[53] Sosuno: That’s my worker. / Not yours to stare at.
[54] ¶ One morning she dumps a bucket at his boots and does not bother pretending it slipped. He laughs. Then he says it like it is nothing.
[55] Sosuno: Watch it. / Or don’t. Drown. Whatever.
[56] Jumong: Hey. / You’re pretty when you’re mean. / Like— actually. Sorry. Not sorry.
[57] Sosuno: Ha—!? / Who’s— pretty, what— / It’s not like that!! / Big idiot. Go. Go go—
[58] Jumong: Going. Going. / Sleeve’s wet. Thanks.
[59] ¶ He wrings the sleeve on the way to the shed. She waits until the yard is empty. Then she hides her whole face in the dusty-rose, red to the hairline, whispering idiot at nobody.
[60] ── SCENE: Upstairs ──
[61] ¶ She does not stay in the yard. Chin still up, she takes the loft stairs two at a time like a woman with grain to count. The window faces the millet: his shirt off, red silk knotted at the hip, a back doing work. Whose son he is can wait. The muscles cannot.
[62] ¶ Another afternoon. The dusty-rose is hiked, her thighs apart on the timber, one hand over her mouth and the other talking to the part of her that does not run a hunt: **Little Sosuno**.
[63] Sosuno: Idiot. Don’t grin in my head. / This is your fault, big idiot.
[64] Sosuno: Little Sosuno… you’re hungry today aren’t you… / I don’t blame you…. mmm! look at him… / Those big muscles…. chest…. back…. / Ah fuck dripping wet again… / Out hunting for meat… / I want you to fill me up with some of that meat….
[65] ¶ Tabal is in the doorway of the yard, not the loft, and his voice still climbs the stairs.
[66] Yeon Tabal: Sosuno! / West count. Now. / Don’t make me climb.
[67] ¶ She freezes mid-breath. She smooths the dusty-rose, wipes her hands on her sleeve, and takes the stairs with her chin up. By the packed earth she is the chieftain’s eldest again.
[68] Sosuno: West is short two. / I counted. Twice. / Don’t send the exile. He’ll get lost.
[69] Yeon Tabal: He hit the boar. / You just don’t like his back.
[70] Sosuno: I don’t like his anything. / Can we do the millet.
[71] ── SCENE: Other Daughters ──
[72] ¶ Word gets out that the exile hits what he aims at and looks like a sun when he works shirtless. Jolbon women find reasons to fetch water. Other chieftains mention daughters. Sosuno is suddenly everywhere those reasons are. She finds a flaw every time.
[73] A chieftain: My girl can count. / Strong arms. Good hall.
[74] Sosuno: He walks into buckets. / Can’t wring a sleeve. Talks to millet. / You’d be bored in a week. Big idiot. Next.
[75] ¶ He flirts at the wrong well, which is any well she can see from the porch, and the girls laugh too long at a sentence he did not finish.
[76] Teal: Hey big boy~
[77] Jumong: You’re— yeah. Funny. Too funny.
[78] Teal: Don’t look at Sosuno. Look at me.
[79] Teal: Don’t follow me. / Unless you are.
[80] ¶ Teal hikes her hem at his well like a dare, the rope between them a bad idea, and leans hip first on the beam. The timber takes her weight. His ears take the rest.
[81] ¶ A Sosuno-shaped shadow falls across the rim before her voice does. She is holding an empty bucket she does not need. The girls notice the shadow first, and the laugh dies.
[82] Sosuno: Get. Off. / Get off my well.
[83] Sosuno: This well’s ours. / Ditch is that way. / He doesn’t need help. He needs to work.
[84] Jumong: I was just—
[85] Sosuno: You. Shed. / Don’t smile at them. / Don’t smile at me either.
[86] ¶ He waits until the girls are gone. Then he does not go to the shed. He follows her to the grain post and says it like weather.
[87] Jumong: So. / You keep chasing them off.
[88] Sosuno: BECAUSE YOU WERE HANGING WITH THOSE OTHER BITCHES—
[89] Jumong: The well girls. That chieftain’s kid. You told her I talk to millet.
[90] Sosuno: BECAUSE YOU DO— / WHO ASKED YOU— / I don’t— they’re in the WAY— / This is MY yard— MY well—
[91] Jumong: Okay. Okay. / You’re screaming. / I’m just asking why I can’t say hi.
[92] Sosuno: DON’T HI THEM. / DON’T HI ME. / BIG IDIOT. GET— get off my post—
[93] ¶ She is screaming mad and pink to the hairline and everyone on the porch can hear the hide crack. He grins. That is worse. She leaves him the post. The well she keeps for tomorrow.
[94] ── SCENE: The Well ──
[95] ¶ They keep meeting there as if the rim were a coincidence.
[96] Jumong: Rope’s being a villain. / Want me to—
[97] Sosuno: Pull or don’t. / Talking doesn’t fill it. / Don’t look at my face. / …Sosuno. / There. Now pull.
[98] Jumong: Sosuno. / Cute name. / Your ears are pink.
[99] Sosuno: Wind. / Don’t— look. / You’re so dumb. Pull.
[100] ¶ He keeps ending up thirsty at the same hour. She keeps being there. On the fourth morning he stops pretending the rope is the problem and kisses her at the well-beam.
[101] ¶ She does not pull away first. When she turns, the dusty-rose is wet at the waist from the rope, and she looks back over her shoulder.
[102] Sosuno: You— / How dare you. / My father’s well— / I will kill you. / After. Move.
[103] Jumong: You kissed back. / Just saying.
[104] ¶ He takes the full bucket and actually goes. She stands at the rim until he is a red speck at the shed. Then both hands over her face, furious, shaking.
[105] ¶ She has been collecting him: a thread, a fletch, a length of well-rope, a scrap of his headband, folded into a cloth behind the grain-porch post. He finds it. He holds it up.
[106] Jumong: Hey. / Mice don’t fold headbands. / You hide these like a thief.
[107] ¶ She goes so red the dusty-rose looks pale. She snatches and misses.
[108] Sosuno: Those are— inventory. / Trash. I’ll burn them. / Don’t grin. If you grin I— give it—
[109] Jumong: You’re keeping a little me in a cloth. / Want it back so you can steal it again?
[110] Sosuno: Keep— ha— keep you? / Go get kept somewhere else. Buyeo. Somebody’s keeping a lamp lit for you there, right? A wife with a lamp. / I’m not your— I’m not anybody’s spare bucket.
[111] ¶ He stops smiling. Not angry. Done. He doesn’t lie about the lamp. He has never once lied to her, which is its own kind of problem. He unslings the bow and lays it on packed earth at the well-rim. Then he walks.
[112] Jumong: She told me to run. I ran. / I’m not gonna stay in your yard as something you hide behind a post. / Keep the bow. Tell the millet thanks.
[113] ¶ She does not call stay. She picks the bow up too fast: the bow her father could not bend. She bends it. One arrow. The timber well-beam beside his ear takes it. He stops.
[114] Sosuno: Wait— wait wait— / Don’t. Don’t turn around. / If you look I can’t—
[115] ¶ The confession comes like a tooth she has been biting since the porch. She talks to the dirt, the bow, anything but his mouth.
[116] ¶ The bird pin comes out in her own fingers. Her hair falls in a sheet, and she sits in the dirt with the bow by her knee and talks into the ground, because his face is a luxury she has not paid for.
[117] Sosuno: I don’t— I don’t like you.
[118] Jumong: Then I’m going.
[119] ¶ Then he grins, smaller than the yard grin, asking.
[120] Sosuno: I wasn’t going to say it. / I was gonna let you leave. Stupid. Fine. / Then you put the bow down and I— / I want you. There. Stay. / Don’t make me— I can’t twice. / Big idiot. Other ear. I swear.
[121] Jumong: Hey. Hey I’m here. / Look. Still here. / Come here. You’re shaking.
[122] ── SCENE: The Grain Room ──
[123] ¶ They do not make it to a feast. The grain-room lamp is closer than pride.
[124] Jumong: Hey. / Numbers later. / Your throat’s brighter than the lamp. Sorry. Not sorry.
[125] Sosuno: I am not your wife yet. / Don’t— my hands. / Counting hand or me. / …Big idiot. / It’s not like that.
[126] Jumong: From the first look. / Buyeo was a hall’s idea. This one’s mine. / Give me your mouth… first. / Country later.
[127] Sosuno: Then take it. / Don’t put a price on it. / I already lost the count.
[128] Sosuno: Now come here before I take it back.
[129] ¶ She hits his chest, once, not hard enough. Then she is on his mouth like she is angry at it.
[130] ¶ The dusty-rose hiked, she braces against the sacks with her back to him, pulls him in by the collar and tells him she hates him in the same breath. Then she feels the weight of him, and the hate gets specific. Love and spite in one grip.
[131] Sosuno: It won’t— ah— fit—
[132] Jumong: Hate me then. / Harder. / God you’re— look at you.
[133] Sosuno: Look— look at you— that chest— that back— those hips I watched from the loft— / That sound. Wet. Slap. That’s— that’s Little Sosuno, she’s— ah— dripping, she— / Take it. That sexy— man meat— I said take it and— destroy my tight little ass— / Beat her up. Beat up Little Sosuno till she’s just wet. Nothing left. That’s all she is—
[134] Jumong: Little Sosuno. / Cute. / I’ve got both of you.
[135] Sosuno: Don’t NAME her don’t— ah— she can hear— she likes it she likes it— / Deeper. The meat. All of it. Don’t you dare pull out— / AHH— DON’T STOP— / DUMB BIG IDIOT—
[136] ¶ He spends himself in her against the grain sacks, and she bites his shoulder so she will not have to hear herself. It does not help. The loft-voice is still in the room.
[137] Sosuno: I didn’t— you didn’t hear destroy— I don’t talk like— / Little Sosuno isn’t— I don’t have a— / Forget it. Get out. Don’t look at me.
[138] Jumong: I heard. / You can talk like that. / It’s you. It’s hot. I’m keeping you. Both.
[139] ¶ Later the lamp has burned down to a bead, and he is still holding on to her as if she were something that might spill.
[140] Jumong: Hey. / You’re beautiful. / Water. You want?
[141] ¶ He goes for water. The door shuts. She lasts three breaths. Then she slides down the sacks with both palms over her mouth, scarlet, furious at a word he already left. Beautiful.
[142] ── SCENE: The Hundred Paces ──
[143] Yeon Tabal: The pine. / Hundred paces. Now. / Hit, he eats. Miss, I throw him. / I am not pleased. I am also not blind.
[144] ¶ The pine stands a hundred paces off across packed earth. Sosuno grips the porch rail, knuckles white, chin up.
[145] ¶ The best men hit bark. Tabal hits the knot. Jumong splits Tabal’s arrow down the shaft, and the hall hears the wood cry.
[146] Jumong: …Yeah. / Still here.
[147] ¶ Then Tabal laughs, short and unwilling.
[148] Yeon Tabal: Eat. / Road can wait. / My daughter bent your bow, I hear. I couldn’t—
[149] Sosuno: The bow is the bow. / Don’t. / I only— lost the count. / Big idiot. Stop smiling.
[150] Yeon Tabal: Ha. / River was supposed to take him. Daughter ran after it. / Sosuno. You picked. You keep. No feast. / Jumong. Hurt her, bow won’t save you. / Eat. Stay. Grumble like the rest of us.
[151] ¶ Tabal sets a vermilion cord where a feast would have been, a short red line, two people who have already spent the night.
[152] ── SCENE: Five Tribes ──
[153] ¶ Jolbon is five roofs that will not share a yard. Cousins cut cousins over a ditch, a ford, a winter store. Jumong watches it for a week and then says it in the hall, easy, the way he hauls sacks.
[154] Jumong: You keep cutting each other. / A ditch is not a country. / I crossed a river on turtles. You fight over who owns the mud.
[155] Yeon Tabal: …Watch your mouth. / Those are my cousins. / They have been mine longer than you have been dry.
[156] Jumong: Then make them one hall. / Five fires, one roof. / Or keep the ditches. I can leave a bow on dirt again.
[157] ¶ He does not conquer them. He walks the five yards with the same grin he used on Sosuno. At the worst ditch, two cousins stand with a knife each. Jumong climbs down between them and sits in the mud, bow unstrung.
[158] Crow cousin: Out of the ditch, slave. / This is family.
[159] Jumong: Okay, okay. I’m just sitting. / Nice ditch. Who dug it?
[160] Cliff cousin: …Our grandfathers. Together.
[161] Jumong: Huh. Together. / So they could share a shovel, and you two can’t share a puddle.
[162] ¶ Nobody says anything for a while. Then the Crow cousin laughs, because the alternative is looking stupid, and the knives go back in the belts.
[163] ¶ What he calls a talk, the valley will call the first summit of the five tribes. For once the smoke agrees.
[164] ¶ That week three men ride into Jolbon on one very fat horse.
[165] Oi: You said fatten him up. / We fattened him up.
[166] Jumong: Okay. Okay. He’s beautiful. / …He can’t run anymore, can he.
[167] Mari: Can’t run. Can’t climb. Eats like a hall. / Took us a month to find you. Where’s our roof?
[168] ── SCENE: The First King ──
[169] [WEDDING Sosuno + Jumong]
[170] ¶ After the marriage the five tribes sit in Tabal’s hall and do the thing they hate more than a ditch: they agree. They vote Jumong first king. Nobody remembers him asking; the grin had already become a roof.
[171] [CARD Jumong]
[172] Yeon Tabal: …Fine. / King, then. / If the ditches start again I will say I told you. / Eat. Stay. Wear it.
[173] Jumong: I will. / Not for the chair. / For the roof.
[174] ¶ Sosuno is the first queen of a country that still smells like millet. The cord is still new. The sacks have not learned to be tribute.
[175] [CARD Sosuno]
[176] ── SCENE: Dawn in the Cavern ──
[177] ¶ Later he goes back to the mouth in the hill to pray, the way a man prays when a hall has named him and he still does not quite believe the name. At dawn the light breaks through.
[178] Jumong: Father! / If you’re listening— they made me king. Me. Of a whole valley. What am I supposed to do with it?
[179] ¶ Gold where the dark had been, and too tall for a lamp. Haemosu lets himself be seen at last: silver-white hair, the sun’s hour delayed on purpose, looking at his son the way he once looked down from a chariot rail.
[180] Haemosu: Jumong…. my son…
[181] Jumong: Father… are you even listening to me?
[182] Haemosu: It is to build a new world. / Build a world of your own…. my son…!
[183] ¶ He comes out of the cavern a king the valley already voted for, and a son who finally saw the face that had been the hour. This morning is only a roof, a grin, and a gold break in the stone.
[184] ── SCENE: The Moon ──
[185] ¶ Thirteen winters pass. Word comes from Buyeo. Yuhwa has stopped. The hall that took her in keeps the body. The door that opens next is not a mortal door.
[186] ¶ Heat in a room that had gone cold. Gold where the lamp had failed. **Haemosu** is simply there — chariot left in the yard like a horse someone could not bear to stable.
[187] Haemosu: Yuhwa. / I didn’t give this to my little brother. / Your hand.
[188] Lady Yuhwa: You’re late. / The copper room… stayed warm. Even when you weren’t in it.
[189] Haemosu: That time I came down. / This time you come up. / There’s an empty seat. On the side where I set.
[190] Lady Yuhwa: That light… it isn’t the one I looked up at from the shallows. / It’s cold. / Still… across from you is fine.
[191] Haemosu: Then come. / The chariot yields the night.
[192] ¶ He does not ask a question. She takes the hand that once could not let go of her. Buyeo keeps a grave. Its records say a river-daughter died. The sky, which keeps poorer records, has a moon the next night.
[193] ¶ Jumong spends the rest of his life driving the western commanderies from the river valleys, and the country grows the way countries grow in old stories: one bowshot, one bride, one sworn brother at a time. Later halls will call him **Dongmyung**, Bright of the East. The walls just call him the Holy King.
[194] ── SCENE: Yodong ──
[195] ¶ In the burned shrine at Yodong, the lamp is down to a bead. Gesomun has told it badly, with his boots on, the way his family always tells it.
[196] 👰: So nobody gave her to him. / Sosuno. She picked him. She shot at him.
[197] Yeon Gesomun: Shot at him, then married him. The women in my family are like that. / Tabal couldn’t bend that bow, you know. We’ve been sore about it for seven hundred years.
[198] 👰: Then why do they give him girls? Why me?
[199] Yeon Gesomun: Because the first time a valley handed him a girl, the valley turned into a country, and the walls held. / Scared towns remember that half. They forget she did the picking.
[200] 👰: …So I can pick.
[201] Yeon Gesomun: Pick, then.
[202] ¶ She takes off the bride’s crown and sets it on the floor under the chain mail, carefully, the way you put down something borrowed. Then she walks out into the ash, toward whatever is left of her mother’s street.
[203] Yeon Gesomun: …Holy King. / You big idiot. Look what they do in your name.
[204] ¶ **Back in Surabol, the queen is failing and the council must name who's next. It only takes one hand to lock the door…!**
